title: Chapter 107 — The Warehouse, Returns & Reverse Logistics
intro: Receiving discipline, the returns machine, and recycling obligations.

sections.title: Receiving Discipline
sections.content:
Every product that enters the warehouse should be inspected at receiving. Check for shipping damage — dents, scratches, crushed corners. Document anything before the product goes to the floor or into delivery staging.

Damage discovered at receiving is the manufacturer's problem. Damage discovered at delivery is your problem. The 60 seconds spent inspecting at the dock saves hours of customer complaints and return processing.

sections.title: The Returns Process
sections.content:
Returns happen. Product defects, wrong models, buyer's remorse, delivery damage. Each one has a different process and a different financial impact.

Defective returns go back to the manufacturer under warranty. Wrong model returns are usually a sales or order entry error — log them so you can fix the process. Buyer's remorse returns may incur a restocking fee — handle with empathy. Delivery damage returns require documentation and a replacement order.

Every return should be logged with the reason. Patterns tell you if a product has issues, if a rep is misselling, or if your discovery process is failing on a specific category.

sections.title: Environmental Obligations
sections.content:
Haul-away units must be disposed of properly. Refrigerants in fridges and A/C units are regulated — they cannot be vented. Many jurisdictions require certified recycling for appliances.

Know your local regulations. Know your store's recycling partners. The customer should never have to think about what happens to the old unit — that is part of the service you provide.
